$description: Motion ledger — the deck's choreography in the Design Tokens Community Group format. Every token here is a CSS custom property declared on :root in src/app/globals.css, so any reason written about timing cites a token path rather than a bare millisecond. The global prefers-reduced-motion block neutralises all of them (duration AND delay clamped, iteration 1), so no consumer needs its own guard. Durations are short by intent: this is an instrument panel visited dozens of times a day, not a stage.

instant.$description: State flips only — hover, toggle, focus ring. Short enough that the control feels wired directly to the pointer.

quick.$description: Popover and menu entrance. Matches the pre-existing .mast-panel measurement (0.18s), so the header's instrument cover and the deck's own surfaces move at one tempo.

base.$description: Page entrance — the deck's heartbeat, used by every .deck-enter child. Long enough to read as an arrival, short enough that a page opened forty times an hour never feels gated.

slow.$description: The single hero reveal per screen. Reserved: one slow element per page is a focal point, two is a queue.

ambient.$description: A self-running loop's period — the deck's weather, and a different species from the ladder above. The four durations preceding it are all RESPONSES: something was triggered, so someone is waiting, and long reads as lag. Nobody triggered this one, so nobody waits on it, and a breath at --motion-dur-base (320ms) would read as a stutter rather than a tide. Every infinite animation cites this token or drift, never a hand-picked millisecond — measured before this token existed, the deck ran thirty-one concurrent loops at periods as short as 0.18s, which on a 60Hz display is a repaint every eleventh frame, forever.

drift.$description: The slowest ambient weather — decorative fields only. Long enough that it is felt rather than watched, which is why it is reserved for surfaces carrying no informational content: a figure that must be read should never sit on top of a drift.

step.$description: Gap between siblings in a sequence. Eight steps consume 315ms — still inside one --motion-dur-base, so the last block lands before the first is done being read. Delays are capped at the eighth child; past that the stagger is latency with better manners.

rise.$description: Travel distance for every entrance. Small on purpose: the move should register as 'arrived', not as a lurch. Measured against the pre-existing mast-rise (6px), so the header and the deck share one amplitude.

out.$description: Decelerate — the surface arrives and settles. Used by every entrance. Matches .slide-in-top and .mast-rise, which already carried this curve.

inout.$description: Symmetric — for loops that must not read as arriving or leaving.

spring.$description: Slight overshoot, for instruments that snap into a detent. Already proven by .mast-compass-tile:hover; carried here so the deck can borrow the same feel without restating the curve.

phase.$description: Perfectly symmetric and flat at both ends — for a loop whose direction reverses mid-cycle, where --motion-ease-inout's asymmetry (0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) would read as a hitch at the turn. Belongs to the ambient ladder; every entrance keeps --motion-ease-out.
